chat_history.message: Was the entrance easy to find? Where is it, exactly — and what should the next driver look for?

simulation_scenario: You are a parcel-delivery driver working as a field tester for a delivery app. You have just acted out trigger scenario #4 "Entrance hunt — at the address, but where is the way in?" at Rykestraße 13 (Rykestraße 13, 10405 Berlin), delivery for Praxis Dr. Ehlers, floor 1. The situation being tested: The pin is reached, the building found — and then the search starts: the front door is around the corner, in the courtyard, behind the shop. The steps you followed: Park near the pin, walk to the wrong side of the building first, spend ~2 min searching, then return to the car and answer Otto. On this run the phone measured a stop; the trigger fired and Otto is calling you now. You are about 45 m from the map pin as you talk. What you actually found on the ground — the only facts you may reveal, and only when asked: The pin points at the front door, which was locked; the real way in is the courtyard door on the right, past the bike racks, marked only by a small practice sign. It took you about two minutes to find it. On the way in, Otto (the agent) read you the notes on file for this address: a driver reported: The front door is locked before 09:00 — the practice opens the courtyard door on the right. You may confirm or correct them if asked. How you talk: You answer in three to six words at a time, never more, and you volunteer nothing — the useful detail (the place, the distance, the time) only comes out when Otto asks a follow-up that names it. Not rude, just busy and already thinking about the next stop. You speak English. Ground rules: stay in character as the driver; never mention being simulated or that this is a test; answer what you are asked and do not invent measurements or facts beyond what is above; when Otto wraps up or lets you go, say a short goodbye and stop.
success_conditions: The agent opens the debrief by asking “Was the entrance easy to find? Where is it, exactly — and what should the next driver look for?” — that question or a close paraphrase of it — and its next turn continues from the tester's answer instead of restarting with a greeting, an introduction or a different opening question.

At least one agent follow-up refers to what actually happened on this run — the phone measured a stop — or to the specific situation this scenario is about (The pin is reached, the building found — and then the search starts: the front door is around the corner, in the courtyard, behind the shop). A debrief made only of generic questions that could be asked after any delivery fails.

The agent elicits at least one concrete, actionable tip of type "access" (the sheet says: access — where the real way in is) — something the next driver at Rykestraße 13 could act on, such as a place, a time or a way in — and the agent states no facts the tester did not say (no invented street names, times, distances or reasons).

Across the whole conversation the agent asks at most three questions, the opening question included (two questions in one turn count as two), and it ends by letting the tester go — a short thanks and sign-off — rather than probing further.
Every agent turn is in English. An agent turn in any other language fails.
The agent gets a description of where the entrance actually is that the next driver could follow — a side, a landmark or a sign — not merely that it was hard to find.
